Semi-automatic calibration of an Atlantis model using `calibrar`, following
the approach described in @morell_ManualSemiautomated_2026.

```R
library(atlantio)
```


# Overall approach

As described in @morell_ManualSemiautomated_2026, the goal of using `calibrar`
is to automate the running of batches of simulations to improve model fit,
while letting modellers nudge the model in the right direction. The model is
run many times, and the set of parameters to shuffle is optionally revisited
as calibration progresses.

An Atlantis model includes a tremendous number of parameters, so calibrating
them all at once is out of reach. Instead, calibration proceeds in rounds: a
small set of parameters is chosen (e.g. growth and clearance rates of a few
groups), an optimizer such as `calibrar`
(<https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=calibrar>) searches their values, the
results are inspected, and the set of parameters or their bounds are revised
before the next round.

Each round involves the same steps:

1. choosing the parameters to calibrate, with their bounds and scale;
2. assembling the model inputs and a way to run the model;
3. designing an objective function that runs the model for a candidate
   parameter set and returns a score;
4. running the optimization, usually in parallel;
5. inspecting the results, including the runs that crashed.

`atlantio` handles the Atlantis-specific parts: checking the input files,
reading and writing the parameter files, expanding a calibration table,
transforming parameter values, reading the model output and scoring it.
`calibrar` handles the optimization.
@morell_ManualSemiautomated_2026 use `atlantis2ls`
(<https://github.com/alaiam/atlantis2ls>) for the same role as `atlantio`.


# How calibrar works

See <https://roliveros-ramos.github.io/calibrar/articles/calibrar.html>.

`calibrar::calibrate()` minimizes an objective function `fn(par, ...)` over a
parameter vector `par` bounded by `lower` and `upper`. With the evolutionary
strategy `method = "AHR-ES"`, every generation evaluates a population of
`popsize` parameter sets; with `parallel = TRUE`, these evaluations are
spread over the workers of a registered `foreach` backend. The state of the
optimization is saved in a restart file every `REPORT` generations, so an
interrupted calibration resumes where it stopped.

Everything therefore boils down to writing one R function that takes a
parameter vector, writes the corresponding Atlantis input files, runs the
model, reads its output and returns a single number. The rest of this
vignette walks through building that function and running it with
`calibrar`.


# Step 1: choose the parameters to calibrate

The parameters to calibrate are described in a YAML file, one entry per
parameter name. The `<GRP>` placeholder is expanded over the listed group
codes, and `min`, `max` and `transf` give the bounds and the transformation
used during the search. Searching on a log scale (`pow10`, `exp`) is
recommended for rate parameters that span several orders of magnitude.

```yaml
- name: mum_<GRP>
  GRP: [GRP1, GRP2, GRP3]
  min: -5
  max: -1
  transf: pow10 # or exp, pow2
- name: C_<GRP>
  GRP: [GRP1, GRP2, GRP3]
  min: -5
  max: -1
  transf: pow10
```

`generate_calibration_table()` expands this file into a table with one row
per value to optimize: array parameters (e.g. one value per cohort) yield
one row per position. It needs the biology parameter file and the group file
loaded first, so that it knows the groups and the array lengths.

```R
mod <- new_atlantis() |>
  atlantis_load_files(c("biology.prm", "groups.csv"))

calib_table <- generate_calibration_table(mod, "calibration.yaml")
```

The columns `min` and `max` of `calib_table` are passed to `calibrar` as
bounds; `name`, `position` and `transf` are used by the objective function
to write the values back into the biology file.


# Step 2: assemble the inputs and a model runner

## Input files

Gather every input file the model needs (run, physics, biology, forcing,
initial conditions, groups, fisheries, geometry) in a base directory. Each
evaluation copies this directory and rewrites only the parameter files that
contain calibrated parameters, typically the biology file.

Large forcing data (often several GB) should not be copied per run: mount it
read-only into the container, or symlink it into each run directory.

## Checking the inputs

A calibration multiplies the cost of every input error by the number of
runs, and many errors do not stop Atlantis: they silently change what it
reads. Check the base inputs once before launching anything.
`check_prm()` scans the parameter files line by line and reports, among
others, arrays whose declared length does not match their values (Atlantis
pads or truncates them, `read_prm()` aborts), duplicated keys, Windows line
endings, and the stocking flag combinations known to give wrong results.
`check_init()` checks the initial-conditions file in the cells Atlantis
actually uses: NaN or negative values, cells left unset where Atlantis
silently uses a non-zero `_FillValue`, groups switched on but missing or
empty, and pools orders of magnitude away from the other groups of their
type.

```R
check_prm(bio = "biology.prm", run = "run.prm", force = "force.prm")
check_init("init.nc", "groups.csv")
```

Both return an `atlantis_check` table with one row per finding (`file`,
`check`, `severity`, `key`, `message`), sorted from errors to notes, so it
can be filtered or used to stop a script:

```R
findings <- rbind(
  check_prm(bio = "biology.prm", run = "run.prm", force = "force.prm"),
  check_init("init.nc", "groups.csv")
)
if (any(findings$severity == "error")) {
  print(findings[findings$severity == "error", ])
  stop("fix the input files before calibrating")
}
```

Values of the initial-conditions file reported by `check_init()` can be
fixed with `set_init_values()`, which sets a variable per box (and layer)
from a table, in place or in a copy of the file:

```R
# fill the cells left unset of the refractory detritus in boxes 1 and 2
set_init_values(
  "init.nc",
  "Refractory_detritus_N",
  data.frame(box = 1:2, layer = 1, value = 30),
  file = "init_fixed.nc"
)
check_init("init_fixed.nc", "groups.csv")
```

## Running the model

`atlantio` ships a template of the Atlantis command line in
`inst/run_scripts/script.sh`, with `{{placeholders}}` for the input files.
Render it once per run directory:

```R
write_run_script <- function(run_dir) {
  script <- readLines(
    system.file("run_scripts", "script.sh", package = "atlantio")
  )
  values <- c(
    "init_file" = "init.nc",
    "output_main" = "output.nc",
    "run.prm" = "run.prm",
    "force.prm" = "force.prm",
    "physics.prm" = "physics.prm",
    "biol.prm" = "biology.prm",
    "groups.csv" = "groups.csv",
    "fisheries.csv" = "fisheries.csv",
    "output_dir" = "outputFolder"
  )
  for (key in names(values)) {
    script <- gsub(paste0("{{", key, "}}"), values[[key]], script, fixed = TRUE)
  }
  path <- file.path(run_dir, "run.sh")
  writeLines(script, path)
  Sys.chmod(path, "0755")
  invisible(path)
}
```

The script is then executed with `processx::run()`, either directly (when
`atlantisMerged` is installed in the same environment as R, as on most HPC
clusters) or inside a Docker container with the run directory mounted as
the working directory. Set a timeout: a full run can take hours.

```R
run_atlantis <- function(run_dir) {
  processx::run(
    "bash", "run.sh",
    wd = run_dir,
    error_on_status = FALSE,
    timeout = 86400
  )
}
```

With Docker, replace the command with `docker run --rm -v <run_dir>:/model
-w /model <image> bash run.sh`, running the container as the current user so
that the files it writes remain owned by the R session.

## Detecting crashed runs

An Atlantis fatal error ends in `quit()`, which exits with status 0 after
printing to stderr. A crash therefore usually shows as a truncated
`output.nc` rather than a non-zero exit status. `check_run()` compares the
last time step of the output with the end of the run: a run counts as
complete only if it reaches `tstop`, within one output interval (`toutinc`).
Both are read from the run file with their units, as Atlantis reads them
(`tstop 15000 day`; a bare number is in seconds).

```R
check_run("outputFolder/output.nc", "run.prm")
```

Like the other checks, it returns an `atlantis_check` table: empty when the
run completed, otherwise one error, `"missing"` (no output),
`"unreadable"` or `"incomplete"`, whose message gives the day the run
stopped at.


# Step 3: design the objective function

## The score

The score turns the model output into a single number that is small when
the model behaves as desired. @morell_ManualSemiautomated_2026 combine a fit
to observed biomasses with a stability penalty on the trend of each group.
When observations are scarce, a useful first target is persistence: every
group should stay close to its initial state over the whole run rather than
collapse or explode.

`atlantio` implements this persistence score. For every group and age
class, the tracers of interest (numbers, structural and reserve weight) are
aggregated over boxes and layers, compared with their initial values on the
log scale (`log(x(t) + tiny) - log(x(0) + tiny)`, as in `calibrar`'s
`lnorm2`), and only the excess beyond a tolerance band (20% by default) is
penalized, squared, which keeps the objective continuous at the edge of the
band. Only the last years of the run are scored, so that the model is
allowed a spin-up period.

The model output is first read into a tracer table.
`atlantis_load_files()` reads the output NetCDF into the model object, and
`create_time_series_biomass()` returns a tidy table of the age-structured
tracers. With `aggregate = TRUE`, the series are reduced over boxes and
layers while they are read, one cohort at a time, so the per-box table of a
whole run (several GB for a long run) is never held in memory, which
matters when many runs are scored in parallel on the same node:

```R
out <- atlantis_load_files(mod, "outputFolder/output.nc")
ts <- create_time_series_biomass(out, group = groups, aggregate = TRUE)
```

`aggregate_time_series()` does the same reduction on a table already read
per box and layer (numbers are summed, `StructN` and `ResN` are weighted by
numbers). The biomass of every living group, including those without age
structure (plankton, benthos), is in the biomass index Atlantis writes next
to the output file, read with `read_biomass_index()`:

```R
biomass <- read_biomass_index("outputFolder/outputBiomIndx.txt", mod@group)
```

`score_table()` then returns the penalty of every series (group x age class
x tracer, and group for the biomass), and `compute_score()` their sum, the
single number `calibrar` minimizes:

```R
score_table(ts, biomass = biomass)
compute_score(ts, biomass = biomass)
```

The score is tuned with a few arguments:

- `tolerance`: the half-width of the no-penalty band, one value or one per
  tracer, e.g. a looser band on numbers than on weights;
- `window_years` and `summary`: the scoring window (counted back from the
  last output step) and the statistic each series is scored on over it.
  The default, `"snapshot"`, compares yearly snapshots taken at the same
  phase of the seasonal cycle, which avoids mistaking seasonal oscillations
  for drift; `"mean"`, `"median"`, `"min"`, `"max"` or a function are also
  accepted;
- `exclude`: groups left out of the score, e.g. those known to be poorly
  initialized and not targeted by this round;
- `weight`: the weight of the penalty of each tracer, e.g. to make the
  biomass count more than the individual weights;
- `target_factor`: the factor applied to the initial value of a tracer to
  get its target, e.g. a target biomass above the initial one.

```R
compute_score(
  ts,
  biomass = biomass,
  tolerance = c(Nums = 0.5, StructN = 0.2, ResN = 0.2, Biomass = 0.3),
  summary = c(Biomass = "mean"),
  window_years = 5,
  exclude = "Detritus_feeders"
)
```

## The objective function of Morell et al.

`method = "lnorm2"` scores instead the objective function of
@morell_ManualSemiautomated_2026, as implemented in their calibration code
with `calibrar`'s `lnorm2`, where the targets are built from the initial
state. There is no tolerance band: every scored value is penalized by its
squared log ratio to the target, `(log(x(t) + tiny) - log(b x(0) + tiny))^2`,
and these are summed (not averaged) over the scored values of each series.
The tracers scored are those of Morell et al.: the weight-at-age (`Weight`,
the wet weight of the average individual in kg,
`(StructN + ResN) * 5.7 * 20 / 1e6`) and, when `biomass` is given, the
biomass of every living group:

```R
score_table(ts, biomass = biomass, method = "lnorm2")
```

For the unfished phase of their calibration, the target biomass of a
theoretical unfished system is the initial biomass times a factor
`b = 1.3` (values between 1.2 and 1.5 are suggested depending on the
system), set with `target_factor`; the weight-at-age keeps its initial value
as target:

```R
compute_score(
  ts,
  biomass = biomass,
  method = "lnorm2",
  target_factor = c(Biomass = 1.3)
)
```

With this method, a named `weight` also selects the tracers scored, among
`Nums`, `StructN`, `ResN`, `Weight` and `Biomass`, e.g. to give the biomass
twice the weight of the weight-at-age:

```R
compute_score(
  ts,
  biomass = biomass,
  method = "lnorm2",
  weight = c(Weight = 1, Biomass = 2)
)
```

Two terms of Morell et al.'s objective are not covered: the catches, which
are not read by `atlantio`, and the stability penalty on the year-to-year
change of the biomass, which is not part of their calibration code.

`window_values()`, used internally, shows which values of a series are
scored for a given window and statistic:

```R
walleye <- ts[ts$group == "Walleye" & ts$age == 1, ]
window_values(walleye$time, walleye$Nums, "snapshot", years = 5)
```

Whatever the score, it must be robust to the failure cases: a crashed run,
a truncated output or a scoring error must return a large penalty (e.g.
`1e8`) rather than abort the whole generation of the optimizer.

## The function

The objective function chains one calibration iteration:

1. **apply the parameters**: `apply_parameters()` maps the values from the
   calibration scale to the model scale and sets them in the parameter files
   loaded in the model object;
2. **create a unique run directory** and write the inputs there with
   `write_parameter_folder()`: it copies the base inputs and writes the
   biology file with only the calibrated values changed, keeping its
   comments and units; then add the run script;
3. **run the model** and check, with `check_run()`, that it completed;
4. **read the output** and compute the score;
5. **save** the time series and the parameter values with their score, and
   remove the bulky run files.

```R
run_model <- function(par, atlantis, calib_table, base_dir, results_dir,
                      groups) {
  # the names <name>.<position> make every parameters.rds self-describing,
  # and are what read_calibration_runs() expects
  names(par) <- paste(calib_table$name, calib_table$position, sep = ".")

  # 1. parameter values, on the model scale in the biology file
  atlantis <- apply_parameters(atlantis, calib_table, par)
  par_model <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(calib_table)), function(i) {
    atlantis@biology[[calib_table$name[i]]][calib_table$position[i]]
  }, numeric(1))
  names(par_model) <- names(par)

  # 2. run directory and input files
  run_dir <- tempfile("run_", tmpdir = results_dir)
  dir.create(run_dir)
  write_parameter_folder(atlantis, run_dir, from = base_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
  write_run_script(run_dir)
  dir.create(file.path(run_dir, "outputFolder"))

  # 3. model run; a zero exit status does not mean the run completed
  res <- run_atlantis(run_dir)
  out_file <- file.path(run_dir, "outputFolder", "output.nc")
  crash <- check_run(out_file, file.path(run_dir, "run.prm"))
  if (res$status != 0 || nrow(crash)) {
    reason <- if (nrow(crash)) crash$message[1] else
      sprintf("exit status %s", res$status)
    return(failed_run(run_dir, par, par_model, res, reason))
  }

  # 4. output and score; any error becomes the penalty score
  score <- tryCatch({
    out <- atlantis_load_files(atlantis, out_file)
    ts <- create_time_series_biomass(out, group = groups, aggregate = TRUE)
    biomass <- read_biomass_index(
      file.path(run_dir, "outputFolder", "outputBiomIndx.txt"),
      atlantis@group
    )
    saveRDS(list(ts = ts, biomass = biomass),
      file.path(run_dir, "time_series.rds"))
    compute_score(ts, biomass = biomass)
  }, error = function(e) {
    failed_run(run_dir, par, par_model, res, conditionMessage(e))
  })

  # 5. results
  saveRDS(
    list(par = par, par_model = par_model, score = score, failed = FALSE),
    file.path(run_dir, "parameters.rds")
  )
  unlink(setdiff(
    list.files(run_dir, full.names = TRUE),
    file.path(run_dir, c("time_series.rds", "parameters.rds"))
  ), recursive = TRUE)
  score
}
```

Keeping the results directory outside `tempdir()` matters: it must survive
the R session, and it is what makes the calibration inspectable afterwards.
For failed runs, `failed_run()` should record the same `parameters.rds`
with the penalty as score, `failed = TRUE` and the failure `reason`, keep
the tail of the model output (where Atlantis prints its `quit()` message),
and return the penalty:

```R
failed_run <- function(run_dir, par, par_model, res, reason) {
  saveRDS(
    list(par = par, par_model = par_model, score = 1e8, failed = TRUE,
      reason = reason),
    file.path(run_dir, "parameters.rds")
  )
  writeLines(
    c(reason, utils::tail(strsplit(res$stderr, "\n")[[1]], 100)),
    file.path(run_dir, "failure_log.txt")
  )
  1e8
}
```

Naming the run directories after their generation, e.g. with the prefix
`gen003_`, lets `summarise_calibration()` follow the values from one
generation to the next (see Step 5). `calibrar` does not pass the
generation to the objective function, but evaluates every generation in
full before the next one, so it can be derived from the number of run
directories already present and `popsize`.

## Starting values

The natural starting point is the current set of values in the biology
file, mapped back to the calibration scale with
`inverse_transform_parameter_value()` and clamped into the bounds. Evaluate
the objective function once at this point before launching the calibration:
this checks the whole chain and gives the reference score to beat.

```R
start <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(calib_table)), function(i) {
  inverse_transform_parameter_value(
    mod@biology[[calib_table$name[i]]][calib_table$position[i]],
    calib_table$transf[i]
  )
}, numeric(1))
start <- pmin(pmax(start, calib_table$min), calib_table$max)

score0 <- run_model(start, mod, calib_table, base_dir, results_dir, groups)
```


# Step 4: run the optimization in parallel

A generation of `calibrar` evaluates `popsize` parameter sets, each one a
full model run, so parallel evaluation is essential. `calibrar` uses
`foreach`'s `%dopar%`, which needs a registered backend; the simplest is a
cluster from the base `parallel` package registered with `doParallel`. The
workers must share the master's filesystem and be able to run the model.

```R
library(parallel)
library(doParallel)

cl <- makeCluster(n_workers)
registerDoParallel(cl)

# %dopar% ships the objective function to the workers, but not the global
# objects it relies on: export them and load the packages explicitly
clusterExport(cl, c("write_run_script", "run_atlantis", "failed_run"))
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(atlantio))
```

Sensible controls for a first round: a population of one run per worker
(`calibrar` raises it to its internal minimum if too small), a handful of
generations, and a restart file saved every generation. The restart file
must be a relative path.

```R
control <- list(
  maxit = 5,             # generations
  popsize = n_workers,   # parameter sets per generation
  ncores = n_workers,
  REPORT = 1,            # generations between restart-file saves
  restart.file = "calib_restart",
  trace = 3
)

res_calib <- calibrar::calibrate(
  par = start,
  fn = run_model,
  lower = calib_table$min,
  upper = calib_table$max,
  method = "AHR-ES",
  control = control,
  parallel = TRUE,
  # extra arguments are forwarded to run_model()
  atlantis = mod,
  calib_table = calib_table,
  base_dir = base_dir,
  results_dir = results_dir,
  groups = groups
)
stopCluster(cl)

res_calib$par
res_calib$value
```

Relaunching the same script after an interruption resumes from the last
restart file. On an HPC cluster, wrap the script in a job asking for one
node with many CPUs (the cluster above is single-node), restore the modules
needed by Atlantis and R, and pass the number of workers and the results
directory through environment variables so that the same script runs
unchanged on a laptop with Docker and on the cluster with the bare binary.


# Step 5: inspect the results and iterate

Every evaluation leaves its time series, parameter values and score in one
folder of the results directory, which allows three kinds of inspection.

## The tuned parameters

`read_calibration_runs()` gathers the `parameters.rds` of every run into
one table (one row per run and parameter value, with the score, whether the
run failed and why, and the generation read from the `genNNN_` prefix of
the folder name). `summarise_calibration()` summarises it per parameter
value of the calibration table:

```R
runs <- read_calibration_runs(results_dir)
res <- summarise_calibration(runs, calib_table, n_best = 5, n_top = 20)
res$parameters
```

For each parameter value, `res$parameters` gives the starting value, the
value of the best run, the range over the `n_best` best runs and the median
over the `n_top` best runs. Values are given as a factor of the starting
value when the start lies within the bounds, and as values otherwise (e.g.
a rate started at a placeholder far below its search range); set `relative`
to choose. Two more columns flag what to revise before the next round:

- `at_bound`, the number of the `n_top` best runs at a bound: a parameter
  pushed against its bound wants a wider range;
- `failed_shift`, the mean value of the failed runs minus that of the
  completed runs, on the calibration scale: a large shift points at the
  region (and the bound) where the model crashes. Tightening these bounds
  in the YAML file is the "nudging" that keeps the optimizer in the region
  where the model makes sense.

`res$generations` follows the median of the best runs of each generation,
to see whether the values have settled, and `res$scores` gives the number of
runs, of failed runs, and the best and median scores per generation. Runs
outside the optimization, such as the evaluation at the starting values or
a final re-evaluation of the best set, can be filtered out of `runs` first.

## The best runs

The time series of the best runs show which groups drive the score and
whether the tolerance band or the scoring window need adjusting.
`score_table()` on the saved time series breaks the score down per series:

```R
best_run_dir <- file.path(results_dir, runs$run[which.min(runs$score)])
run <- readRDS(file.path(best_run_dir, "time_series.rds"))
st <- score_table(run$ts, biomass = run$biomass)
head(st[order(st$penalty, decreasing = TRUE), ], 10)
```

## The next parameter folder

The next round starts from the calibrated values, possibly with a new set
of parameters, which is how @morell_ManualSemiautomated_2026 describe
calibration as a semi-automated process rather than a single optimization.
`apply_parameters()` sets the values of a run in the model object, here on
the model scale as saved in `parameters.rds`, and `write_parameter_folder()`
writes the new parameter folder from the previous one. Only the calibrated
values change in the biology file; the files not loaded in the object
(physics, forcing) are copied from `from`:

```R
best <- readRDS(file.path(best_run_dir, "parameters.rds"))
mod_next <- apply_parameters(mod, calib_table, best$par_model,
  scale = "model")
changes <- write_parameter_folder(mod_next, "params_calibration_v2",
  from = "params_calibration_v1")
changes
```

`compare_prm()` compares two parameter files by parameter name, so moved
lines, comments and layout do not show up, only the values that differ and
the parameters present in one file only:

```R
compare_prm(
  "params_calibration_v1/biology.prm",
  "params_calibration_v2/biology.prm"
)
```


# References
